<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par155 />Thus after a determinate substantive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=צוּרִי אֶֽחֱסֶה־בּוֹ|translate=my rock in which I take refuge}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=1}}; in Jb 3<sup>3 ''a''</sup> also, the omission of the article with {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}} is only a poetic licence. After an indeterminate substantive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=6}}, last clause but one; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=2}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|155|k}}
In this case also the retrospective word is not infrequently suppressed, giving rise to extremely short, bold expressions, such as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=1}} ''look unto the rock'' {{GHGheb|text=חֻצַּבְתֶּם}} (whence) ''ye were hewn, and to the hole of the pit'' {{GHGheb|text=נֻקַּרְתֶּם}} (whence) ''ye were digged''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=27}} ''the devices'' (where-with) ''ye act violently against me''.—A retrospective adverb is suppressed in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=19}} ''where is the way'' (to the place where) ''the light dwelleth?'' cf. 38:24.

{{GHGmargin-letter|155|l}}
Rem. 1. The omission of the retrospective word occurs most frequently in relative clauses which are governed by the construct state of a preceding substantive (especially an expression of time) and hence are virtually in the genitive. In addition to the instances already given in {{GHGpar|130|d}}, cf. the following: after {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=56|verse=10}}; after {{GHGheb|text=מִיּוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=2}}; after simple {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=56|verse=4}} ({{GHGheb|text=יוֹם אִירָא|translate=on the day}} when ''I am afraid''); after {{GHGheb|text=בְּעֵת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=27}} ({{GHGheb|text=בְּעֵת הֵחֵל הָֽעוֹלָה|translate=at the time}} when ''the burnt offering began''); 20:22, 24:11, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=17}}; after {{GHGheb|text=לְעֵת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=35}}; after {{GHGheb|text=עַד־עֵת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=2}}; after {{GHGheb|text=מֵעֵת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=4|verse=8}} ''thou hast put gladness in my heart more than'' (their gladness) ''at the time'' (when) ''their corn and their wine are increased''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|155|m}}
2. The agreement ({{GHGpar|138|d}}) of the retrospective pronoun with a pronominal regens in the 1st or 2nd person also takes place in a simple co-ordinated relative clause in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=14}} ''who art thou'' (that) ''criest?'' Cf., however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=19}} ''we are become'' as they ''over whom'' ({{GHGheb|text=בָּם}} not {{GHGheb|text=בָּ֫נוּ}}) ''thou no longer bearest rule''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|155|n}}
'''3.''' Occasionally—chiefly in poetic or otherwise elevated style—even ''independent'' relative clauses are simply co-ordinated with a regens, whereas we should expect them always to be preceded by a demonstrative pronoun, on the analogy of the examples in {{GHGpar|138|e}}. The suppressed pronoun would stand—

(''a'') As subject, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=24}} ''an abomination'' (is he) ''that chooseth you'' (but read perhaps {{GHGheb|text=לִבְחֹר}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=13}}, cf. {{GHGpar|152|u}}.

(''b'') As object, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=2}}, with a retrospective pronoun; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=2|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=וְכִסָּה|translate=and}} him ''that covereth'' (or read {{GHGheb|text=וְכֹסֶה|translate=?}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=12}} ''I delivered... the fatherless also, and'' him ''that had none to help him''.

(''c'') In the genitive governed by a substantive (cf. {{GHGpar|130|d}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלַח־נָא בְּיַד־תִּשְׁלָֽח|translate=send, I pray thee, by the hand of}} him ''whom thou wilt send'', i.e. by the hand of some one else; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=5}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=32}}, verbal-clauses after {{GHGheb|text=אֵשְׁרֵי|translate=O the happiness of}} the man, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=81|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=141|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=14}}; after {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=4}}, but we must certainly read here, with the Samaritan and LXX, {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־אֲשֶׁר יֶשׁ־לוֹ}} as in verses 5 and 8; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=4}}; verbal-clauses after {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=30|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=1|verse=5}}.

(''d'') Governed by a preposition; so verbal-clauses after {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=8}}; after {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} (=''to the place where''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=12}}, but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=20}} before the same<section end=par155 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
